about: In the prayers at the foot of the altar, Psalm 42 in the Vulgate numbering (Psalm 43 in Hebrew) is said alternately by the priest and server. The antiphon “Introíbo ad altáre Dei” precedes it and is repeated after the doxology. In Masses for the Dead, and at Masses of the season from Passion Sunday through Maundy Thursday, the psalm is left out with its antiphon and the Confíteor follows at once.

seg.nr: At Masses for the Dead, and at Masses of the season from Passion Sunday through Maundy Thursday, the psalm, the Glória Patri and the repetition of the antiphon are omitted. After In nómine Patris, the antiphon and the Adiutórium, the Confíteor follows at once.
The priest says the psalm alternately with the ministers.

seg.tr: Judge me, O God, and decide my case against an unholy people. Deliver me from an unjust and deceitful man.
For You, O God, are my strength. Why have You rejected me, and why do I walk in sorrow while the enemy oppresses me?

ex.w030: The Latin form can also be feminine, but the corresponding Hebrew and Greek forms are masculine.

seg.tr: Send forth Your light and Your truth. They have led me and brought me to Your holy mountain and into Your dwelling places.
And I will go to the altar of God, to God, who gladdens my youth.

ex.w064: The Hebrew text speaks of joy, while “youth” appears in the Septuagint, which the Latin follows here.

seg.tr: I will praise You on the lyre, O God, my God. Why are you sad, my soul, and why do you disturb me?

ex.w067: Latin says literally “I will praise to Thee”. English requires the direct form “I will praise Thee”.

seg.tr: Hope in God, for I will yet praise Him. He is the salvation of my countenance and my God.

ex.w088: Latin says literally “I will praise to Him”. English requires the direct form “I will praise Him”.

seg.tr: Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit.

ex.w095: The sense is: may glory be.

seg.tr: As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.
I will go to the altar of God.
To God, who gladdens my youth.
